method: Zero searches. The Phase-1 URL (web.cvent.com/.../summary) is NOT a SERMACS page - it is the ACS Regional Meetings Resource Portal for organisers - and sermacs.org redirects to acs.org, which is behind an Incapsula block. Probing edition domains found https://www.sermacs2025.org/ : 'Joint Meeting of SERMACS/SWRM 2025 - The 76th Southeastern and 81st Southwest Joint Regional Meeting of the American Chemical Society', 26-29 Oct 2025, DoubleTree by Hilton Orlando at SeaWorld. Extracted twice (pdftotext -layout and -raw) and parsed in Python: track the current SESSION TYPE, and for each line matching ^\s*(\d{1,3})\s+(\d{1,4})\b(?!\s*(AM|PM|:)) record the second number as a paper number under that type (unnumbered 'Break' rows never match). Layout: 1,450 unique papers (Oral 762, Poster 688), highest 1,467, 17 gaps (107, 146, 204, 230, 307, 308, 322, 378, 439, 458, 628, 1080, 1123, 1167, 1204, 1218, 1234); raw: 1,438. Only Oral/Poster sessions carry paper numbers. EXCLUDED: plenary, workshop, networking and special-event sessions. NOT excludable: invited symposium speakers are not flagged in MAPS output, so 1,450 is an upper bound on contributed. CAVEAT FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: 2025 was a JOINT meeting with the Southwest Regional Meeting (SWRM), so this figure covers two ACS regions; a standalone SERMACS year would likely be smaller, and a separate SWRM row (if one exists on the sheet) is the same event in 2025 - de-duplicate. Language searched: English (US). VERDICT: counted 900-1,499 -> BORDERLINE. Rung 9 not needed.

conference: Gordon Research Conference on Energetic Materials
abstracts: ~120 INFERRED FROM ATTENDANCE, NOT COUNTED (rung 9 - a hard 200-attendee cap x ~60% poster-presenting for a HYBRID invited-talk-plus-poster programme)
spot_checks: the 2026 Energetic Materials GRC programme page itself shows the shape: named invited talks in single-track sessions with 'Discussion Leader' framing, plus one Poster Session and one Poster Previews slot per day - no numbered abstract series anywhere
no open call for abstracts exists: attendance is by application and chair selection
character_evidence: No open call for abstracts - 'scientists must apply to the conference and be selected by the conference chair to attend the meeting' (https://www.grc.org/about/). The talk programme is wholly invited; the only contributed element is the poster session, and GRC's MyGRC account text ('print a receipt (which includes verification that you are presenting a poster)') shows poster presentation is the normal condition of attending.
programme_evidence: Single-track invited talk sessions each followed by discussion, with a daily Poster Previews slot and a 2-hour Poster Session; posters are not published as a numbered abstract book.
ratio_rationale: Judged 60% for THIS conference, and the judgement barely matters because the cap dominates. GRC's own account page treats presenting a poster as the normal condition of attending ('verification that you are presenting a poster'), and the daily Poster Previews slot means posters are the whole contributed channel - so the share of the room that submits something is high, far above a trade-fair or CME meeting. But the invited talk programme is closed, senior attendees and the GRS students are not all poster presenters, and there is no published abstract book, so 60% rather than 90%. At the 200 cap that is ~120, and even at 100% it is 200 - two full orders of magnitude below the ~900 floor, so no plausible ratio changes the verdict.
method: Zero searches. Rungs 1-8 were not worth spending on and rung 9 settles the row outright, because GRC publishes a HARD SIZE CAP: https://www.grc.org/about/ states 'GRC organizes over 395 Gordon Research Conferences (GRCs) and Gordon Research Seminars (GRSs) per year' and 'Each conference is limited to 200 attendees; scientists must apply to the conference and be selected by the conference chair to attend the meeting.' Fetched that page and the 2026 conference page https://www.grc.org/energetic-materials-conference/2026/ with curl and read the full text - no abstract book, no numbered abstract series, no open call. The 200 figure is a CAP (an upper bound on attendance), not a measured headcount, so it is tagged UNSPECIFIED; using it as if it were the actual attendance is generous to the row and still puts the inferred figure at ~120. 200 attendees cannot yield 900 contributed abstracts at ANY conversion ratio, so this is positive evidence of size, not absence of evidence: OUT. Language searched: English (GRC is a US body publishing only in English). NOTE for the orchestrator: the same cap applies to all ~395 GRCs and GRSs, so whether GRC is carried as one census row or exploded into hundreds changes only the number of deleted rows, never the census total.
